newsitem.title: UK: Britain's GUS posts first profit fall in 48 years.
newsitem.headline: Britain's GUS posts first profit fall in 48 years.

text.p: British retailer Great Universal Stores, best known for its Burberry classic clothing, Thursday reported its first fall in half-year profits in 48 years.
The company said the drop in profits, which fuelled a fall in its stock, was partly attributable to its flagging mail order business.
The group, Britain's premier mail order business, said it saw no significant signs of a second half upturn.
Higher costs and the strong British pound were behind the slip in earnings of the group for the first time since 1949.
Pretax profits fell to 235.6 million pounds ($382 million) from 237.5 million pounds ($383 million) in the six months to Sept. 30. Sales rose to 1.21 billion pounds ($!.95 billion) from 1.20 billion.
Chairman Lord Wolfson of Sunningdale said trade was still difficult in the home shopping division, which saw both sales and profits fall in the first half.
Traders said the damage done by a strong pound to earnings from GUS's overseas retailing interests, including Burberry, also hit the stock.
Last month GUS broke with its deeply conservative past by buying U.S. information services firm Experian for $1.7 billion, its first acquisition in more than two decades.
The change of pace followed the arrival of Lord Wolfson of Sunningdale as chairman in August, taking over from his older cousin Lord Wolfson of Marylebone.
There has been speculation of more changes to come, especially as the new chief is also chairman of highly successful fashion retailer Next Plc, which also has a mail order business.
GUS stock fell 22.5 pence (36 cents) to 653.5 pence ($10.54).
